title: [Bug]: qwen3_5_mtp fails to load at tensor-parallel-size >= 2 (drafter weight shape mismatch)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... uv is set ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 15.2.0-16ubuntu1) 15.2.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 4.2.3 Libc version : glibc-2.43 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 (main, Apr 7 2026, 20:45:25) [Clang 22.1.1 ] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-29-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.43 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.2.78 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 2: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 3: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti GPU 4: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 5: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU 6: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Nvidia driver version : 610.43.03 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 Vendor ID: AuthenticAMD Model name: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9955WX 16-Cores CPU(s): 32 NUMA node(s): 1 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 [pip3] numpy==2.3.5 [pip3] torch==2.13.0 [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0 [pip3] transformers==5.15.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.27.1 GPU Topology (relevant pair): GPU0 <-> GPU1: NODE (PCIe, no NVLink) ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` (equivalently `--spec-method qwen3_5_mtp`) fails to load at `--tensor-parallel-size >= 2` for a Qwen3.5-architecture dense model (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, `model_type: qwen3_5`) with a shape-assertion crash inside the MTP drafter's weight loader. It works fine at TP=1 (modulo a separate, likely-unrelated OOM covered at the bottom, on a 24GB GPU specifically). The crash reproduces with both the Qwen3.5-specific and the generic MTP method name, so the method name isn't the variable — it looks like the drafter (loaded via a code path separate from the main model, in `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`) ends up with an effective tensor-parallel/world size that's inconsistent with the main model's requested TP degree. **Model:** a Heretic-abliterated, NVFP4-quantized (via NVIDIA Model-Optimizer's `hf_ptq.py`, `--qformat nvfp4`) finetune of `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (dense, `mtp_num_hidden_layers: 1`). The base model's config declares `mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings: false`. Not a MoE model, no `--quantization moe_wna16`/GPTQ/AWQ involved, so this isn't #39475's `moe_wna16` MTP KeyError, and I confirmed `packed_modules_mapping` in `qwen3_5_mtp.py` is correct (`["q_proj","k_proj","v_proj"]` / `["gate_proj","up_proj"]`), so this isn't #35031's `gate_up_proj` copy-paste bug either — those are the two closest prior issues I could find and neither matches. The checkpoint's own `mtp.*` tensors were preserved unmodified from the original release (spliced back in from the raw upstream checkpoint after an unrelated finetuning step dropped them — `transformers`' `Qwen3_5PreTrainedModel._keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected = [r"^mtp.*"]` means any `AutoModel.from_pretrained()` round-trip silently discards `mtp.*` weights, so they have to be reattached from the original checkpoint afterward). I want to flag this clearly in case it's relevant, but I don't believe it's the cause of the crash below — see the "ruled out" list. #### Repro ```bash vllm serve \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' ``` Also reproduces identically with `--spec-method qwen3_5_mtp --spec-tokens 3` in place of the JSON `--speculative-config` form. #### Observed ``` (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id) (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 989, in weight_loader_v2 (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] param.load_merged_column_weight( (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] File ".../vllm/model_executor/parameter.py", line 175, in load_merged_column_weight (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape (Worker_TP1 ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:912] AssertionError ``` Both `Worker_TP0` and `Worker_TP1` crash identically, on the first fused (`qkv_proj` or `gate_up_proj`) weight loaded for the MTP block's single decoder layer (`mtp.layers.0.*`). #### Diagnosis With `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the MTP block's `mlp.down_proj` (a plain row-parallel weight, loaded through a different, less strict code path than the fused-column weights) loads *successfully* right before the crash, with logged shape `torch.Size([5120, 4352])`. The raw checkpoint's `mtp.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight` is `(5120, 17408)`. `17408 / 4352 = 4` — not `17408 / 2 = 8704`, which is what correct TP=2 row-parallel sharding should produce. That means the drafter is loading with an effective world size of 4 for at least this tensor, while the rest of the process (main model included) is correctly running at TP=2. The very next fused-column weight for the same MTP layer hits the strict `assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape` in `load_merged_column_weight`, which — unlike `down_proj`'s loader — doesn't tolerate the inconsistency. I wasn't able to pin down exactly where inside `llm_base_proposer.py`'s model/parallel-config construction for `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor` the world size diverges — didn't have a local vLLM checkout set up to add print statements at `get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()` in the drafter's construction path specifically. The `down_proj` shape is solid, reproducible evidence of *that* the divergence happens; not *why*. #### Ruled out - **Not the method name / CLI form**: identical crash with `--spec-method qwen3_5_mtp` and with the generic `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` form. - **Not an NVFP4-quant-exclusion config issue**: tested directly against `ModelOptNvFp4Config.is_layer_excluded()` in a Python shell with the checkpoint's real `hf_quant_config.json` — `mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj` and all sibling MTP linear-layer names correctly resolve as excluded from NVFP4 quantization. The destination parameters are being allocated as plain unquantized `nn.Parameter`s, same as the main model's, so this isn't a quantization-format/exclude-list matching problem. - **Not an actual architecture incompatibility.** I initially assumed the checkpoint's `q_proj` being unusually wide (12288, which is 48 attention-heads'-worth against a nominal 24-head config) was the root cause. That's wrong: the *main* model's decoder layers have the identical `q_proj=(12288,5120)` shape (likely related to `attn_output_gate: true` in the config) and load/serve correctly at TP=2. `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor.__init__` explicitly constructs its single layer via the exact same `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer` class the main model uses for its full-attention layers, so this shape is not MTP-specific and not the bug. - **Disappears entirely at TP=1** — all weight loading succeeds, including everything that crashes at TP=2. (At TP=1 on a single 24GB GPU I then hit a separate `torch.OutOfMemoryError` while constructing `Qwen3_5MTP`'s `ParallelLMHead`, which persisted even after cutting `--max-model-len` from 262144 down to 32768 with no change in the reported memory figures — suggesting the MTP drafter may be allocating its own dedicated `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` regardless of the checkpoint's `mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings: false`, though I haven't confirmed that with an actual memory snapshot at the crash site, just arithmetic that happens to line up — `vocab_size=124160, hidden_size=5120` gives ~1.27GB per duplicated embed/lm_head tensor. Flagging this separately since it may or may not be related; happy to open it as its own issue if it turns out to be unrelated to the TP crash above.)
